tests.code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from cart_api import app

client = TestClient(app)

import pytest

@pytest.mark.parametrize("units,unit_cents,subtotal", [(1, 1, 1), (9, 10000, 90000)])
def test_subtotal_inclusive_endpoints(units, unit_cents, subtotal):
    response = client.post("/estimate", json={"units": units, "unit_cents": unit_cents})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["subtotal"] == subtotal

tests.name: 609b3c7b-e67d-4cba-92af-915cc33ee03d.py
tests.code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from cart_api import app

client = TestClient(app)

import pytest

@pytest.mark.parametrize("units,unit_cents,member,expected", [
    (1, 549, False, {"subtotal": 549, "discounted": 549, "delivery": 0, "total": 549}),
    (1, 549, True, {"subtotal": 549, "discounted": 439, "delivery": 60, "total": 499}),
    (1, 625, True, {"subtotal": 625, "discounted": 500, "delivery": 0, "total": 500}),
    (1, 1, True, {"subtotal": 1, "discounted": 0, "delivery": 60, "total": 60}),
])
def test_pricing_rules(units, unit_cents, member, expected):
    response = client.post("/estimate", json={"units": units, "unit_cents": unit_cents, "member": member})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert {key: body[key] for key in ("subtotal", "discounted", "delivery", "total")} == expected

tests.code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from cart_api import app

client = TestClient(app)

import pytest

@pytest.mark.parametrize("field,value", [
    ("units", 0), ("units", -1), ("units", 1.5), ("units", "2"), ("units", 10),
    ("unit_cents", 0), ("unit_cents", -1), ("unit_cents", 1.5), ("unit_cents", "2"), ("unit_cents", 10001),
])
def test_invalid_quantity_or_price_returns_422(field, value):
    response = client.post("/estimate", json={"units": 1, "unit_cents": 1, field: value})
    assert response.status_code == 422

tests.code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from cart_api import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_valid_response_contains_four_fields():
    response = client.post("/estimate", json={"units": 2, "unit_cents": 250})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert {"subtotal", "discounted", "delivery", "total"}.issubset(response.json())

Feature: Estimate subtotal
Scenario Outline: Subtotal uses inclusive valid integer endpoints
Given an estimate request with units <units> and unit_cents <unit_cents>
When I POST the request to /estimate
Then the response has HTTP 200
And subtotal equals <subtotal>

Examples:
| units | unit_cents | subtotal |
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 9 | 10000 | 90000 |

Feature: Estimate pricing
Scenario Outline: Member and non-member estimates apply documented pricing rules
Given a request with units <units>, unit_cents <unit_cents>, and member <member>
When I POST the request to /estimate
Then subtotal is <subtotal>
And discounted is <discounted>
And delivery is <delivery>
And total is <total>

Examples:
| units | unit_cents | member | subtotal | discounted | delivery | total |
| 1 | 549 | false | 549 | 549 | 0 | 549 |
| 1 | 549 | true | 549 | 439 | 60 | 499 |
| 1 | 625 | true | 625 | 500 | 0 | 500 |
| 1 | 1 | true | 1 | 0 | 60 | 60 |

Feature: Estimate request validation
Scenario Outline: Invalid units or unit price are rejected

| field | value |
| units | 0 |
| units | -1 |
| units | 1.5 |
| units | "2" |
| units | 10 |
| unit_cents | 0 |
| unit_cents | -1 |
| unit_cents | 1.5 |
| unit_cents | "2" |
| unit_cents | 10001 |

Feature: Estimate response shape
Scenario: Valid request returns all four pricing fields
Given a valid request with units 2 and unit_cents 250
When I POST the request to /estimate
